annotations.title: Who leaue the right way.
annotations.text: Generally this deſcription of wicked men, agreeth to al that committe and perſiſt in mortal ſinne, whether they vvalked right at anie time before or no; but moſt eſpecially shevveth the properties of heretikes: <mn>[1]</mn> who forſake and leaue the direct, ancient, beaten, knovvne vvay of the Catholique Church, <mn>[2]</mn> and teach nevv obſcure doctrines, not heard of, or not approued in our forefathers time. <mn>[3]</mn> Secondly (v. 14) they glorie in their ovvne deuiſes, and reioyce in moſt vvicked thinges, as in ſeducing multitude of peoples, to rebel againſt their Catholique Princes, and other Superiors ſpiritual and temporal, in breaking vovves; in deſpiſing good vvorkes; truſting to only faith, and that not the Catholique faith of al true Chriſtians, but euerie one his particular perſvvaſion, that himſelf is iuſt, & shal be ſaued, vvhich by their ovvne doctrin, none is bond to beleue of an others ſtate, but of his ovvne only. In ſo much that the chiefeſt point of a Proteſtants imagined faith, is not a general Article, which al do or should beleue, but a moſt particular and ſingular phantaſie, which each one muſt conceiue of himſelf, or herſelf. <mn>[4]</mn> Thirdly (v. 16.) Hereſie, called here the ſtrange and forrene woman, tempereth her vvordes, to pleaſe the itching eares of her auditorie, framing her doctrine to the humour of thoſe, vvhom she ſeeketh to peruert. The ſame vvhich the Apoſtle ſaith in other vvordes, by ſvveete ſpeaches and benedictions they ſeduce the hartes of innocents. <mn>[5]</mn> Fourthly (v. 19.) Thoſe that do enter into error of hereſie, shal not returne, that is, very hardly and rarely returne into the right vvay of life; <mn>[6]</mn> the reaſon whereof the ſame Apoſtle yeldeth, becauſe an heretike is condemned by his ovvne iudgement. <mn>[7]</mn> For being in error, and admitting no iudge but himſelf, he parteth from the Church, excludeth the meanes of better inſtruction, & through his erronious iudgement, remaineth in damnable opinion, and ſo in the ſtate of damnation.

notes.text: Foure markes of an heretike. 1. He forsaketh the knowen faith.
2. He glorieth in his ovvne inuention.
